answer: Each identity runs one reef survey station at a harbor and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a key-signed profile for its reef, with its summit elevation, corrected by the harbor tide table. An auditor recomputes it from tide table and log; a missing profile, reused crest shape, or wrong elevation burns the bond. A fake needs a new survey: first 31, k-th 31+5(k-1), 1000th 5026, so 1000 fakes pay 2,528,500 with 70,000 at risk. A rented-transect ring fails: one crew cannot make distinct summit profiles for two keys in one window. An honest station pays 31 once and keeps its bond.
